topic: Raylib CoreData Architecture and Frame Lifecycle
extracted_claim: raylib uses single CoreData global struct with nested Window, Storage, Input, Time sub-structs. Window tracks screen/render/FBO dimensions, flags, position. Input has Keyboard (key states + press queue), Mouse (position, buttons, wheel), Touch, Gamepad arrays. Time has current/previous/update/draw/frame/target measurements. Frame lifecycle: InitWindow → BeginDrawing (update time) → draw calls → EndDrawing (rlDrawRenderBatchActive, SwapScreenBuffer, frame time control, PollInputEvents). Platform abstraction via include of platform-specific rcore_<platform>.c files.
implementation_relevance: HSE has no core/window system yet. raylib's CoreData pattern is a reference for global engine state.

document_reference: rcore.c: BeginMode2D(), BeginMode3D(), BeginTextureMode(), BeginShaderMode(), BeginBlendMode()
extracted_claim: Rendering modes are Begin/End pairs that push/pop matrix state. BeginMode2D: rlDrawRenderBatchActive, rlLoadIdentity, apply camera matrix. BeginMode3D: switch to RL_PROJECTION matrix, push, set perspective/orthographic, switch to RL_MODELVIEW, apply camera, enable depth test. BeginTextureMode: enable FBO, set viewport, ortho projection. All modes flush render batch before switching. EndMode3D restores projection from stack, disables depth test. Screen scaling applied via screenScale matrix.
implementation_relevance: HSE has no rendering modes. Begin/End pattern with matrix stack is a classic OpenGL approach.

extracted_claim: Shader loading: LoadShader(vsFile, fsFile) reads files, calls LoadShaderFromMemory. Returns Shader struct with id (program) and locs (int array of RL_MAX_SHADER_LOCATIONS). Custom shaders use rlLoadShaderProgram(vsCode, fsCode). Default shader fallback when custom fails. Shader locations bound by name-to-location mapping. TraceLog for diagnostics. Callback system for loadFileData/saveFileData for custom I/O.
implementation_relevance: HSE has basic shader loading. raylib's shader location system is a simpler reference than OpenGL directly.
